scenes.visual: Title card 'What a Negative Is Worth' over a cartoon pond with a sampling bottle. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: BLUE = the scoop, theta (water sample holds DNA); GREEN = capture, gamma (extraction); GOLD = the well, delta (one qPCR run); FILLED TEAL pond = occupied; GREY OUTLINE pond = empty; RED dashed horizontal line = the 5% stop line. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Ponds, bottles, tubes and wells are flat labelled cartoons; bars and gauges are computed from the lesson's formula and labelled 'computed'; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: When every test from a pond comes back negative, what have you learned? Is the species gone? At fifty-three English ponds, newts were seen while the water was being sampled. Yet thirteen percent of those samples, about seven, showed no newt D N A.
scenes.caption: When every test from a pond comes back negative, what have you learned? Is the species gone? At 53 English ponds, newts were seen while the water was being sampled. Yet 13% of those samples, about seven, showed no newt DNA.
scenes.visual: A cartoon newt swims in a pond as a hand fills a bottle. On-screen counters build: '53 ponds: newts seen during sampling', then '13% of samples (about 7): no amplification'. A flat qPCR trace stays flat beside the bottle. Source tag: 'Buxton and colleagues, 2021'.
scenes.narration: When every test from a pond comes back negative, what have you learned? Is the species gone? At 53 English ponds, newts were seen while the water was being sampled. Yet 13% of those samples, about seven, showed no newt DNA.

scenes.tts: A survey is a series of nets with holes. First, D N A must be in the water you scoop. That chance is theta. Second, the extraction must capture it. That chance is gamma. Third, one q P C R well must amplify it. That chance is delta.
scenes.caption: A survey is a series of nets with holes. First, DNA must be in the water you scoop. That chance is theta. Second, the extraction must capture it. That chance is gamma. Third, one qPCR well must amplify it. That chance is delta.
scenes.visual: Three stacked nets appear one by one as each is named: BLUE net labelled 'the scoop (θ)', GREEN net 'capture (γ)', GOLD net 'the well (δ)'. A small gold DNA dot drops from the top; it passes the blue net, then slips through a hole in the green net and falls out the bottom. Schematic.
scenes.narration: A survey is a series of nets with holes. First, DNA must be in the water you scoop. That chance is theta. Second, the extraction must capture it. That chance is gamma. Third, one qPCR well must amplify it. That chance is delta.

scenes.tts: Together, the nets give one number, q. It is the chance that one water sample detects a pond that really is occupied. Here we use a round number: q is one half.
scenes.caption: Together, the nets give one number, q. It is the chance that one water sample detects a pond that really is occupied. Here we use a round number: q is one half.
scenes.visual: The three nets slide together and collapse into a single dial labelled 'q: one sample's chance of detecting an occupied pond'. The needle settles at '0.5'; tag 'round number for this film'.
scenes.narration: Together, the nets give one number, q. It is the chance that one water sample detects a pond that really is occupied. Here we use a round number: q is one half.

scenes.tts: Now picture a hundred ponds like yours. Before sampling, we think twenty of them hold the species. Those are teal. The other eighty, in grey, are empty. With no false positives, an empty pond always tests negative.
scenes.visual: A 10 x 10 grid of 100 small pond icons fades in: 20 FILLED TEAL (label 'occupied: 20, the prior'), 80 GREY OUTLINE (label 'empty: 80'). The teal ponds are scattered, not clustered. A vertical bar at right, labelled 'P(occupied | all negative)', fills to 20% (computed). RED dashed line on the bar at 5%.
scenes.narration: Now picture a hundred ponds like yours. Before sampling, we think twenty of them hold the species. Those are teal. The other eighty, in grey, are empty. With no false positives, an empty pond always tests negative.

scenes.tts: Sample every pond once. Half the occupied ponds light up as detections and leave the pile. Ten occupied ponds stay hidden among eighty empty ones. The share of negative ponds still occupied drops to eleven percent.
scenes.visual: A bottle icon sweeps across the grid ('sample 1'). 10 of the 20 teal ponds flash bright and slide off to a side tray labelled 'detected'. 10 teal ponds remain, now dimmed as 'hidden', among 80 grey. Counter: '10 hidden / 90 negative'. The side bar drops from 20% to 11% (computed).
scenes.narration: Sample every pond once. Half the occupied ponds light up as detections and leave the pile. Ten occupied ponds stay hidden among eighty empty ones. The share of negative ponds still occupied drops to eleven percent.

scenes.tts: Now take a second, independent sample from every pond that is still negative. How many hidden occupied ponds will remain? And what share of the negative ponds will still hold the species?
scenes.visual: A second bottle hovers over the grid, labelled 'sample 2: new water'. The 10 dimmed teal ponds pulse. Two question tags float: 'hidden ponds left?' and 'share of negatives occupied?'.
scenes.narration: Now take a second, independent sample from every pond that is still negative. How many hidden occupied ponds will remain? And what share of the negative ponds will still hold the species?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; caption 'Predict: how many hidden ponds, and what share?'

scenes.tts: Half of the ten hidden ponds are caught. Five stay hidden, among eighty-five negative ponds. The share falls to about six percent. A third sample leaves two and a half hidden ponds on average, about three percent.
scenes.caption: Half of the ten hidden ponds are caught. Five stay hidden, among 85 negative ponds. The share falls to about 6%. A third sample leaves 2.5 hidden ponds on average, about 3%.
scenes.visual: Sample 2 sweeps: 5 teal ponds flash and leave. Counter '5 hidden / 85 negative'; the bar drops to 5.9% (computed), still just above the RED 5% line. Sample 3 sweeps: counter '2.5 hidden (average) / 82.5 negative'; bar drops to 3.0%, below the line.
scenes.narration: Half of the ten hidden ponds are caught. Five stay hidden, among 85 negative ponds. The share falls to about 6%. A third sample leaves 2.5 hidden ponds on average, about 3%.

scenes.tts: The side bar tracks the chance that a negative pond is still occupied. It falls with every independent sample, but never reaches zero.
scenes.visual: The side bar enlarges to centre as a step plot over 'samples: 0, 1, 2, 3' with values 20%, 11%, 5.9%, 3.0% (computed), RED dashed 5% line across. The steps keep shrinking toward zero but a thin teal sliver stays at each step.
scenes.narration: The side bar tracks the chance that a negative pond is still occupied. It falls with every independent sample, but never reaches zero.

scenes.tts: The grid is the equation. On top sit the hidden occupied ponds: the prior, times the chance an occupied pond misses every time. Below sit all the negative ponds: the empty ones, plus those hidden ones.
scenes.visual: The grid morphs term by term into: P(occupied | all negative) = prior x m / [(1 - prior) + prior x m]. The dimmed teal ponds fly into the numerator 'prior x m'; the grey ponds fly into '(1 - prior)' in the denominator, joined by a copy of the teal ones as '+ prior x m'. Label under m: 'm = chance an occupied pond misses on every sample'.
scenes.narration: The grid is the equation. On top sit the hidden occupied ponds: the prior, times the chance an occupied pond misses every time. Below sit all the negative ponds: the empty ones, plus those hidden ones.

scenes.tts: Two numbers here are set by us, not measured by this survey. One is the prior, how likely occupancy was before sampling. The other is the stop line, here five percent. Change either, and the samples you need change.
scenes.visual: Two dials beside the equation, both tagged 'set by us': 'prior' (set at 20%) and 'stop line' (set at 5%, the RED dashed line). Schematic.
scenes.narration: Two numbers here are set by us, not measured by this survey. One is the prior, how likely occupancy was before sampling. The other is the stop line, here five percent. Change either, and the samples you need change.

scenes.tts: The count also assumes no false positives. Each pond stays occupied or empty for the whole survey. And each sample is an independent try.
scenes.visual: Three checkbox lines appear under the equation: 'no false positives', 'occupancy fixed during the survey', 'samples independent'.
scenes.narration: The count also assumes no false positives. Each pond stays occupied or empty for the whole survey. And each sample is an independent try.

scenes.tts: So a negative never proves absence. Each negative sample multiplies the hidden ponds by the miss chance. The empty ponds stay put. But is every test you run a new try?
scenes.visual: The grid returns briefly: the dimmed teal 'hidden' ponds shrink by half with each sample while the 80 grey ponds stay unchanged; then the step plot, each step labelled 'independent negative sample'. On the last line, a cluster of twenty gold wells under one blue bottle appears with a small question mark, then fades.
scenes.narration: So a negative never proves absence. Each negative sample multiplies the hidden ponds by the miss chance. The empty ponds stay put. But is every test you run a new try?

scenes.visual: End card (standard Hex card), one line only: 'Each negative sample multiplies the hidden ponds by the miss chance.'
